mainTopic: Who keeps a consecrated ancestral field for the family, and what happens to it at the יובל
overview: The גמרא explains the פסוקים in ויקרא 27 about a consecrated ancestral field. A ברייתא learns from 'לְאִישׁ אַחֵר' that if the son redeems the field it stays in the family. A brother counts as 'another man'. The reason is that a son stands in his father's place for יעידה and עבד עברי, and even יבום only happens when there is no son. רבה בר אבוה asks about a daughter, and a teaching of דבי רבי ישמעאל shows she counts as an outsider when there is a son. רבי זירא asks whether a woman's husband or her son keeps her field for her, and that question ends in תיקו. רב חסדא rules that a field consecrated less than two years before the יובל still goes to the כהנים, because it can be redeemed. A ברייתא learns from 'אחוזתו' that a כהן who redeemed the field does not keep it; it is divided among all the כהנים. A new משנה then records a three-way dispute about a field nobody redeemed: רבי יהודה says the כהנים take it and pay, רבי שמעון says they take it for free, and רבי אליעזר says they never take it. The גמרא traces רבי יהודה's and רבי שמעון's views to different comparisons of the word 'קדש', and its answer to why רבי יהודה prefers the house continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Explaining the two cases in the verse: owner and treasurer
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that "if he will not redeem" refers to the owner, and "if he sold" refers to the גזבר of הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: The Sages taught: "If he will not redeem the field" is about the owner. "Or if he sold the field" is about the treasurer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that explains, word by word, the פסוק about a consecrated ancestral field. First it tells us who is doing what in each half of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "if he will not redeem" means the original owner (בעלים) never bought the field back from הקדש. The phrase "if he sold" cannot mean the owner, because the field belongs to הקדש now. So it means the treasurer (גזבר) sold it to someone else. In both cases the field goes to the כהנים at the יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that explains the משנה
The owner, here the person who consecrated the field
The treasurer of the Temple's property (הקדש)
An ancestral field that a family inherited

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
"If he will not redeem the field" refers to the owner;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:20

phrases.english: "or if he sold the field" refers to the treasurer.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אִם לֹא יִגְאַל אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה בְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה about a consecrated ancestral field
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "If he will not redeem" refers to the owner; "if he sold" refers to the גזבר.

steps.title: "Another man" excludes the son
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from "לְאִישׁ אַחֵר" that the field goes to the כהנים only when someone other than the son redeemed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: "To another man" means to someone else, but not to the son.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reads the words "to another man" in the פסוק. It says these words exclude the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The field goes to the כהנים at the יובל only if it was sold to "another." If the son of the person who consecrated it redeemed it, the son is not "another," so the field stays in the family. This is the source for the ruling in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: "To another man", the words being explained
To another, but not to the son
The Jubilee year, when fields go back to their owners or, here, to the כהנים

phrases.english: "To another man":
to another, and not to the son.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאִישׁ אַחֵר לְאַחֵר וְלֹא לַבֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק, moving on to its next words
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the son redeems the field, it does not go to the כהנים; "another" excludes the son.

steps.title: Maybe "another" excludes the brother instead
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: why say "another" excludes the son? Perhaps it excludes the brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it means to another and not to the son? Or perhaps it only means to another and not to the brother?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own reading. It suggests that "another" could just as easily be excluding the brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son and a brother are both close relatives. Nothing in the word "another" alone tells us which relative it leaves out. So the ברייתא needs to show why the son is the one excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: "Do you say... or perhaps it is only...", a formula for testing a different reading
Brother

phrases.english: Do you say: to another, and not to the son?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְאַחֵר וְלֹא לָאָח?
phrases.english: Or is it only to another, and not to the brother?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לְאַחֵר וְלֹא לַבֵּן אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְאַחֵר וְלֹא לָאָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading from step 2 by offering a different relative
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does "another" exclude the son or the brother?

steps.title: "Man" already covers the brother, so "another" excludes the son
steps.stepSummary: The word "אִישׁ" already includes the brother, so the extra word "אַחֵר" must be there to exclude the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the verse says "man," the brother is already covered. So what do I learn from "another"? That it is not the son.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The brother is already counted under the word "man," so "another" has to be about the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats each word of the פסוק as teaching something. "אִישׁ" is enough to include the brother as an outsider whose purchase sends the field to the כהנים. The word "אַחֵר" must then add something new, so it leaves out the son.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is already stated", meaning it is already covered by the verse
"How do I give meaning to...", used to find a purpose for an extra word

phrases.english: When it says "man,"
the brother is already stated.
phrases.notes: He means the brother is already included in the word "man," so the brother counts like any outsider.

phrases.english: So how do I give meaning to "another"?
And not to the son.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר אִישׁ הֲרֵי אָח אָמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 and confirms the reading of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "אִישׁ" already includes the brother, so "אַחֵר" must exclude the son.

steps.title: Why treat the son as family and the brother as an outsider?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for a reason: why should the son be included with the father while the brother is left out?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made you include the son and exclude the brother?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a logic question. Even with the word-reading, why does it make sense for the son to count like the father and not the brother?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 gave a reason from the words of the פסוק. Now the ברייתא wants a reason in the law itself for treating these two relatives differently. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: "What did you see?", meaning what is your reason for this choice
To include
To exclude

phrases.english: And what did you see to include the son
and to exclude the brother?
phrases.notes: "Include" here means the son is treated like the father, so the field returns to the family.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַבֵּן וּלְהוֹצִיא אֶת הָאָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the conclusion of step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the logical reason that the son counts like the father but the brother does not?

steps.title: The son stands in his father's place
steps.stepSummary: The son is included because he takes his father's place in two other laws: יעידה of an אמה עבריה and an עבד עברי.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include the son, because he stands in place of his father for designating a maidservant as a wife, and for a Hebrew slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the son is like a continuation of the father. We see this in two other areas of הלכה where the son steps into his father's shoes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father who bought an אמה עבריה can do יעידה, making her a wife for his son, but not for his brother. An עבד עברי keeps serving the son after the father dies, but he goes free if the brother inherits him. Since the son takes the father's place there, he is treated like the father here too.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands in place of his father
Designating an אמה עבריה as a wife
A Jewish indentured servant
A Jewish maidservant, the one who can receive יעידה

steps.whatToRemember: A field consecrated by its owner goes to the כהנים at the יובל if the owner did not redeem it or the גזבר sold it to "another man." The son is not "another": the word "אִישׁ" already covers the brother, "אַחֵר" excludes the son, and the son stands in his father's place for יעידה and עבד עברי.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the brother is excluded because he is a distant relative. The point is the opposite: the son is so close that he counts as the father himself, while the brother, close as he is, counts as "another man."
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source and the reason for the משנה's rule that a field the son redeemed goes back to the family at the יובל.

phrases.english: I include the son,
since he stands in place of his father
for designation and for a Hebrew slave.
phrases.notes: "Designation" means a father making the Jewish maidservant he bought into a wife for his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי הַבֵּן שֶׁכֵּן קָם תַּחַת אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The son stands in place of his father for יעידה and for an עבד עברי, so he is treated like the father here too.

steps.title: Maybe the brother should be included instead
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes back: the brother should be the one included, because he takes his brother's place for יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, I should include the brother, since he stands in his brother's place for levirate marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own answer from step 6. It points to one law where the brother, not the son, takes the dead man's place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said the son is like the father because of two laws. Now a counter-example appears: in יבום, the brother steps into his dead brother's place. So maybe the brother, not the son, should share the father's status for the field.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite is true
Levirate marriage: a brother marries his dead brother's childless widow
Stands in the place of; takes over for

phrases.english: On the contrary,
I should include the brother,
phrases.notes: Include him with the father, so that if the brother redeems the field, it does not go to the כהנים.

phrases.english: since he stands in his brother's place for levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי אֶת הָאָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 6 by offering a counter-law that favors the brother.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 6 that the son, not the brother, takes the father's place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יבום shows the brother taking the dead man's place, so the brother may deserve to be included instead.

steps.title: יבום only happens when there is no son
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers: יבום only applies when there is no son, so even here the son outranks the brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there ever levirate marriage except where there is no son? If there is a son, there is no levirate marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the brother argument. The brother only does יבום because there is no son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brother's role in יבום is not a sign that he is stronger than the son. A son cancels יבום completely. So יבום itself shows the son comes first, and the son stays included.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there ever...? (a rhetorical question meaning 'surely not')
In a case where

steps.whatToRemember: The son always comes before the brother. Even יבום, the brother's 'special' law, only exists when there is no son.

phrases.english: Is there ever levirate marriage
except where there is no son?
But if there is a son, there is no levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ יִבּוּם אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turns the challenger's own example around: יבום depends on there being no son.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The brother takes the dead man's place in יבום, so he should be included.
steps.terutzMaskana: יבום only exists when there is no son, so the son still ranks first and is the one included.

steps.title: Why not just count the reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed this answer. The son has two supporting laws and the brother only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him simply derive it from the fact that here there are two reasons, and here there is only one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's method. It suggests an easier answer: two reasons (son) beat one reason (brother).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son had two laws behind him: יעידה and עבד עברי. The brother had only one: יבום. So why argue about יבום at all, when simple counting would do?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it (from a simpler source)
Two
One

phrases.english: But let him simply derive it
from the fact that here there are two,
phrases.notes: The two laws for the son from step 6: יעידה of an אמה עבריה, and עבד עברי.

phrases.english: and here there is only one!
phrases.notes: The single law for the brother, which is יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ, דְּהָכָא תַּרְתֵּי, וְהָכָא חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why step 8's answer was needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's choice to answer with the יבום argument.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two supporting laws should outweigh one, so the longer answer seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The עבד עברי reason depends on the same יבום logic
steps.stepSummary: Counting doesn't work, because the עבד עברי reason is itself learned from the same point: יבום only happens when there is no son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the law of the Hebrew slave is also derived from this very refutation: Is there ever levirate marriage except where there is no son?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The son doesn't really have two independent reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that the son, and not the brother, steps in for the father with an עבד עברי is not stated in the Torah. It is learned from the same idea: יבום only happens when there is no son. Without that idea there is no 'two versus one,' so the יבום answer is the real foundation.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; an argument that knocks down a claim
He derives it; he learns it

steps.whatToRemember: The son outranks the brother because יבום only exists when there is no son. That idea is the base for the whole argument.

phrases.english: Because the law of the Hebrew slave
from this very refutation also
phrases.notes: He means the line from step 8, which the גמרא now quotes again.

phrases.english: is what he derives it from:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ יִבּוּם אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בֵּן?
phrases.english: Is there ever levirate marriage except where there is no son?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּעֶבֶד עִבְרִי מֵהַאי פִּירְכָא נָמֵי הוּא דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the two reasons are not independent; one depends on the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son has two separate reasons against the brother's one, so simple counting should settle it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עבד עברי reason rests on the יבום logic, so that logic is the real basis.

steps.title: Can a daughter keep the field for her father?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה asks whether a daughter who redeems the field keeps it for her father, like a son. He gives reasons for both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה asked: A daughter, what is the law? Does she keep the field for her father? Since for levirate marriage a son and a daughter both exempt equally, she keeps it. Or perhaps, since for inheritance a daughter is like 'another person' when there is a son, she does not keep it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבה בר אבוה asks whether a daughter counts like a son for redeeming the field, and lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: for יבום, a daughter cancels יבום just like a son, so she should count like him. Side two: for inheritance, a daughter gets nothing when there is a son, so she is like 'another person' and does not count. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked; he raised a question with no clear answer yet
What is the law?
She keeps (the field) in place for someone
They exempt (free the widow from יבום)
Inheritance
Or perhaps (introduces the other side)

steps.confusionAlert: A daughter is not 'like another person' in general. She is only like that for inheritance, and only when there is a son.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Avuh asked:
A daughter, what is the law
that she keep the field for her father?
Since regarding levirate marriage,
a son and a daughter exempt equally,
she keeps it,
or perhaps
since regarding inheritance,

phrases.aramaic: בַּת בִּמְקוֹם בֵּן כִּי אַחֵר דָּמְיָא
phrases.english: a daughter, where there is a son, is like 'another person',
phrases.notes: This links back to the word 'אַחֵר' in the פסוק from step 2.

phrases.english: she does not keep it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: בַּת מַהוּ שֶׁתַּעֲמִיד שָׂדֶה לְאָבִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the son-versus-brother rule to ask about a new relative, the daughter.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a daughter who redeems her father's consecrated field keeps it for him like a son does.
steps.whyThisMatters: It tests which comparison decides who is 'like the father': יבום, where daughter and son are equal, or inheritance, where they are not.

steps.title: A daughter counts as an outsider when there is a son
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from דבי רבי ישמעאל shows that when there is a son, a daughter is treated like an outsider. So she does not keep the field for her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: anyone who counts as 'another person' when a son exists does not keep the field for the owner. A daughter, when there is a son, also counts as 'another person'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבה בר אבוה's question from Step 11. It uses a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that only someone who stands in the son's place keeps the field for the owner. A daughter does not inherit when there is a son, so in that case she is like any outsider. Because of that, her redemption does not keep the field for her father.

keyTerms.meaning: Another person, an outsider who does not keep the field for the owner
Where there is a son

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Anyone who is 'another' where there is a son,
and this one too, where there is a son,
is like another.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about a daughter raised in Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When there is a son, a daughter is like an outsider and does not keep the field for her father.
steps.whatToRemember: Only someone who truly takes the son's place keeps the field. When there is a son, a daughter does not.

steps.title: Who keeps a woman's field for her: husband or son?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether a woman's husband or her son keeps her consecrated field for her. Each side has a reason, and the question is left unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asks: if a woman consecrated her field, who keeps it for her by redeeming it? Is it her husband, since he inherits from her? Or is it her son, since he inherits even property that was only due to her, as well as property she actually held? The question stands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks a new question about a woman's field. The גמרא cannot answer it and ends with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband has a strong claim because he is her heir while he is alive. The son has a different strong claim: he inherits even property she was only due to get (ראוי), not just property she already held (מוחזק). Since both are a kind of heir, it is unclear which one counts as standing in her place.

keyTerms.meaning: Keeps the field in the owner's possession by redeeming it
He inherits from her
Property that was due to come to a person but was not yet in hand
Property a person already actually held
Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the son wins just because he inherits more kinds of property. The husband also has a real claim, and that is why the question ends in תיקו.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asks:
A woman: who keeps the field for her?
Does the husband keep it for her, since he inherits her,
or perhaps the son keeps it for her,
since he takes what is due as well as what is held?
phrases.notes: A son inherits even what his mother was going to get. A husband inherits only what she already had.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same idea of 'standing in the owner's place' and applies it to a woman's field.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the husband or the son keeps a woman's consecrated field for her.

steps.title: A field consecrated less than two years before יובל
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא about a field consecrated less than two years before the יובל and not redeemed. Does it go to the כהנים?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked רב חסדא: if someone consecrated his field less than two years before the יובל, does it go out to the כהנים?
steps.whatsHappening: This opens a new topic. רמי בר חמא asks whether a field consecrated very close to the יובל goes to the כהנים, like a normal unredeemed field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an unredeemed consecrated field goes to the כהנים at the יובל. A field consecrated less than two years before the יובל is different: it cannot be redeemed with a deduction for the remaining years and must be redeemed at full value. The question is whether this difference also changes what happens at the יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: He consecrated it to the Temple
The Jubilee year, every fiftieth year
It goes out to the כהנים, passing to them at the יובל

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked Rav Chisda:

phrases.aramaic: הִקְדִּישָׁהּ פָּחוֹת מִשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים לִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל,
phrases.english: If he consecrated it less than two years before the Jubilee,
phrases.notes: 'It' is his inherited family field (שדה אחוזה), which he did not redeem.

phrases.english: what is the law: does it go out to the priests?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the question of who keeps the field.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a field consecrated less than two years before the יובל goes to the כהנים if it is not redeemed.

steps.title: רב חסדא spells out the reasoning behind the question
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks what the reasoning is and lays it out. The פסוקים link 'deduction' with 'going out in the יובל', so maybe only a field that can get a deduction goes to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is your thinking? The פסוק says 'And it shall be deducted from your valuation', and then 'And the field, when it goes out in the יובל'. So a field fit for deduction goes to the כהנים, and a field not fit for deduction does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא does not answer right away. He first spells out the reason someone might think the field does not go to the כהנים, which sets up his next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים appear close together. This suggests that going to the כהנים at the יובל applies only to a field that can be redeemed with a deduction. A field consecrated less than two years before the יובל gets no deduction, so by this reading it would not go to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: What is your thinking? He is asking for the reasoning behind the question
'And it shall be deducted from your valuation'
Fit for a deduction: a field whose redemption price is reduced for the years left until the יובל

phrases.english: He said to him: What is your thinking?
'And it shall be deducted from your valuation...'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:18

phrases.english: 'But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:21. Reading these two פסוקים together is what links deduction to going to the כהנים.

phrases.english: one that is fit for deduction: yes;
one that is not fit for deduction: no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רמי בר חמא's question by first spelling out the reasoning behind it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the questioner's reasoning that, since the פסוקים link 'deduction' to 'going out in the יובל', only a field fit for a deduction goes to the כהנים?

steps.title: On the contrary: the field can be redeemed, so it goes to the priests
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא now argues the other side. The פסוק links going out to the כהנים with a field that could have been redeemed. This field could be redeemed, so it should go to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! The פסוק says: 'If he will not redeem the field … the field, when it goes out in the יובל' (goes to the כהנים). And this field also can be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא pushes back on the reasoning he just laid out. He shows a different link in the פסוקים that points the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15, the link was between 'deduction' and 'going out in the יובל', which suggested a field with no deduction would not go to the כהנים. רב חסדא rejects that and points to the link between 'if he will not redeem' and 'going out in the יובל'. Since this field can still be redeemed, his answer is that if it is not redeemed it goes to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to be redeemed; something that can be redeemed

steps.confusionAlert: Step 15 was only רב חסדא spelling out what רמי בר חמא might be thinking. Here, with 'אַדְּרַבָּה', רב חסדא gives his real answer: this field can be redeemed, so if it is not redeemed it goes to the כהנים.

phrases.english: On the contrary,
"If he will not redeem the field..."
"...and the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee" (goes to the priest),
and this field, too, is one that can be redeemed.
phrases.notes: "This field" is the one consecrated less than two years before the יובל, from רמי בר חמא's question.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reasoning of step 15 with the opposite reading of the פסוקים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that only a field that gets a deduction goes to the כהנים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק ties going to the כהנים to the field being redeemable, not to the deduction. This field is redeemable.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'his possession shall be for the priest'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a כהן who redeemed the field. A ברייתא asks why the פסוק needs the word 'אחוזתו'. It explains the concern: maybe the כהן who redeemed it could claim the field as his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if one of the כהנים redeemed it, etc. The Sages taught: why does the פסוק say 'his possession shall be for the priest'? Take a field that would go to the כהנים in the יובל, and one of the כהנים redeemed it. How do we know he may not say, 'Since it goes to the כהן anyway, and it is already in my hands, let it be mine'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It brings a ברייתא that asks what a phrase in the פסוק comes to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a field the owner did not redeem, so in the יובל it would go to the כהנים. Before the יובל, one כהן redeemed it from the Temple treasury. The question is whether this כהן keeps the whole field because he is a כהן and already holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this? What does it teach?
From where do we know?
In my hands; in my possession

phrases.english: If one of the priests redeemed it, etc.
The Sages taught:
"His possession shall be for the priest,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:21

phrases.english: why does the verse need to say this?
From where do we know, about a field that goes out to the priests in the Jubilee,
and one of the priests redeemed it,
from where do we know that he may not say:
"Since it goes out to the priest anyway,
and it is already in my hands, let it be mine"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the word 'אחוזתו' teach? Specifically, may a כהן who redeemed the field keep it for himself in the יובל?

steps.title: A קל וחומר that the priest should keep the field
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a logical argument for the כהן's claim. If he gets a share of other people's fields, surely he should keep the field he redeemed himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it would make sense: if I gain a share in fields belonging to others, shouldn't I all the more so keep my own?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא presents a strong logical argument that the כהן should keep the field. This explains why a פסוק is needed to teach otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the יובל, every כהן gets a share of fields that he never redeemed. This field the כהן redeemed with his own money. The argument says that his claim to his own field should be even stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical; a reasoned argument
Gain ownership of; acquire
All the more so (a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: And it would be logical:
if I gain a share in fields of others,
is it not all the more so with my own?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the logical reason behind the claim raised in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the field is divided among all the כהנים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: a כהן shares in fields he did not redeem, so surely he keeps the field he did redeem.

steps.title: 'His possession' means only his own, so the field is shared among the priests
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'אחוזתו', which means a possession that is truly his. This field is not his. So it leaves his hands and is divided among all the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches 'his possession', meaning a possession that is his own. This field is not his. How so? It leaves his hands and is divided among his brothers, the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. It reads the word 'אחוזתו' to block the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אחוזתו' means only a field that truly belongs to the כהן, like one he inherited, is fully his own. A field he redeemed from הקדש does not count as his אחוזה. So the logical argument is overruled by the פסוק, and the field is shared among all the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: A family-owned field; an inherited landholding
How so? How does this work in practice?
Is divided up

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן who redeemed a consecrated field does not keep it in the יובל. The word 'אחוזתו' teaches that it is not his own, so it is divided among all the כהנים.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "his possession,"
meaning a possession that is his own,
and this field is not his.
How so?
It leaves his possession
and is divided among his brothers, the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֲחוּזָּתוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 and overrides the קל וחומר of step 18 with a reading of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אחוזתו' limits the rule to a field that is truly the כהן's own. A redeemed field is not his, so it is divided among all the כהנים.

steps.title: The new משנה: an unredeemed field at the יובל, opinions of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: If the יובל comes and the consecrated field was never redeemed, רבי יהודה says the כהנים enter it and pay its value. רבי שמעון says they enter it but do not pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: If the יובל arrived and the field was not redeemed, the כהנים enter into it and pay its value to הקדש. This is what רבי יהודה says. רבי שמעון says: they enter into it, but they do not pay.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks what happens to a consecrated field that nobody redeemed when the יובל came, and it gives two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the sugya dealt with a field that someone else redeemed, which goes to the כהנים at the יובל. Here nobody redeemed it at all. Both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון agree the כהנים get the field. They argue only about whether the כהנים must pay its value to הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה'. It marks the start of the משנה.
It was redeemed, meaning bought back from הקדש.
They enter into it, meaning they take possession of the field.
Its value, the redemption money paid to הקדש.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If the Jubilee arrived and it was not redeemed,
the priests enter into it
and give its payment,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Shimon says:
They enter, but they do not give payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הִגִּיעַ יוֹבֵל וְלֹא נִגְאֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves from a field that a כהן redeemed (steps 17-19) to a field that nobody redeemed at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the כהנים take the unredeemed field and pay its value. רבי שמעון: they take it without paying.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the כהנים never take an unredeemed field
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the כהנים neither enter nor pay. The field stays with הקדש and is called an 'abandoned field' through each יובל, until someone else redeems it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: they do not enter and they do not pay. Instead, the field is called 'an abandoned field' until the second יובל. If the second יובל comes and it still was not redeemed, it is called 'abandoned of the abandoned' until the third יובל. The כהנים never enter into it until someone else redeems it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third opinion. רבי אליעזר holds that the כהנים do not get the field at all in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the field goes to the כהנים only if another person redeemed it first, which was the case discussed earlier in the sugya. If nobody redeemed it, it simply stays in הקדש. Each יובל that passes just gives it a 'more abandoned' name.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'abandoned field', one left sitting in הקדש because nobody redeemed it.
'Abandoned of the abandoned', a field that has stayed unredeemed through two יובלות.
Until another person redeems it.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier case. There, someone other than the owner redeemed the field, and then it went to the כהנים. Here nobody redeemed it, and רבי אליעזר says that is exactly why the כהנים cannot take it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
They do not enter and they do not give payment,
rather, it is called 'an abandoned field'
until the second Jubilee.
If the second Jubilee arrived and it was not redeemed,
it is called 'abandoned of the abandoned'
until the third Jubilee.
The priests never enter into it
until another person redeems it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא נִכְנָסִין וְלֹא נוֹתְנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the dispute in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים do not get an unredeemed field. It stays in הקדש until another person redeems it.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה says the כהנים must pay for the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: What is the reason for רבי יהודה's view?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It asks for the source behind רבי יהודה's ruling that the כהנים must pay. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question focuses on the payment. Why should the כהנים have to pay for a field that comes to them at the יובל?

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא. It marks where the discussion of the משנה begins.
'What is the reason?' A request for the source or logic of a view.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first opinion in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for רבי יהודה's rule that the כהנים pay the field's value.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from someone who consecrates a house
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns 'קדש' here from 'קדש' by a consecrated house. Just as a house comes out of הקדש only with money, so too the כהנים get this field only with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'holy' from 'holy' in the case of one who consecrates a house. Just as there it is with money, so too here it is with money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבי יהודה's source is a גזירה שוה, meaning the same word appears in two places and so the rule from one place applies to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'קדש' is used for a house someone consecrates, and that house can only come out of הקדש by paying money. The same word is used for the field that goes to the כהנים at the יובל. So the כהנים, too, can take the field only by paying its value.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns, meaning he derives a rule from another place.
Linking two laws because the same word appears in both.
One who consecrates a house to הקדש.
'Just as there… so too here.' The standard formula for carrying a rule from one case to another.
With money, meaning by paying its value.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's rule that the כהנים must pay comes from a גזירה שוה: 'קדש' by the field and 'קדש' by a consecrated house. In both cases, getting the property out of הקדש requires money.

phrases.english: He derives 'holy' from 'holy'
phrases.notes: The field: ויקרא 27:21. The house: ויקרא 27:14.

phrases.english: from one who consecrates a house,
just as there it is with money,
so too here it is with money.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּמַר ״קֹדֶשׁ״ ״קֹדֶשׁ״ מִמַּקְדִּישׁ בַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'קדש' from a consecrated house: just as the house is redeemed only with money, the כהנים take the field only with money.

steps.title: רבי שמעון learns from the lambs of שבועות
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון compares 'קדש' by the field to 'קדש' by the כבשי עצרת. Those lambs go to the כהנים for free, so the field does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון learns 'holy' and 'holy' from the lambs of עצרת. Just as there it is for free, so too here it is for free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains where רבי שמעון gets his view that the כהנים do not pay for the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה linked the field to a consecrated house, which leaves הקדש only with money. רבי שמעון links the same word 'קדש' to a different place: the two lambs of שבועות. Those lambs are a gift to the כהנים with no payment, so the field also comes to them for free.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy. This shared word is the link between the two cases.
The two lambs brought on שבועות together with the two loaves
For free, without paying

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון use the same word 'קדש'. They do not argue about whether to compare. They argue about which case to compare it to: a house or the lambs.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: The question 'what is his source?' is left out but understood, following the question about רבי יהודה in step 22.

phrases.english: learns 'holy' and 'holy' from the lambs of עצרת,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:20 says the lambs are 'holy to ה' for the כהן'.

phrases.english: just as there it is for free,
so too here it is for free.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, גָּמַר ״קֹדֶשׁ״ ״קֹדֶשׁ״ מִכִּבְשֵׂי עֲצֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's source, side by side with רבי יהודה's source from step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רבי שמעון's source that the כהנים do not pay?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A comparison by the word 'קדש' to the כבשי עצרת, which go to the כהנים for free.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יהודה also learn from the lambs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: the lambs of שבועות are also called 'קדש', so why not learn from them like רבי שמעון?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה too, let him learn from the lambs of עצרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: there is a source that says 'for free', so why does he choose the house, which needs money?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two places share the word 'קדש': the house and the lambs. The גמרא wants a reason why רבי יהודה picks the house over the lambs. Without a reason, his choice looks random.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him learn (derive) it
Also, too

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda too,
phrases.notes: The name in square brackets is added in the corrected wording, so read it as רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: let him learn from the lambs of עצרת!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נָמֵי נֵילַיף מִכִּבְשֵׂי עֲצֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי שמעון's source from step 24 to challenge רבי יהודה's choice in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's choice to learn from the consecrated house (step 23)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The lambs share the same word 'קדש', so there is no clear reason to prefer the house.

steps.title: Learn בדק הבית items from בדק הבית items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: things consecrated for בדק הבית are learned from other בדק הבית things. The answer continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn items consecrated for the upkeep of the בית המקדש...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering why רבי יהודה prefers the house. This line sets up a rule, and the rest of it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The field was consecrated for בדק הבית, the upkeep fund of the בית המקדש. The answer is heading toward the idea that such items should be compared to other בדק הבית items, like the house, not to קרבנות like the lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: We judge, we learn one case from another
Items consecrated for the upkeep of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: We learn items consecrated for the upkeep of the Temple

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Preference for a more similar source (same category of הקדש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lambs and the house are equally good sources, since both say 'קדש'.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בדק הבית item should be learned from another בדק הבית item (completed in the next section).
